card.name: Perkhuli
card.profile: Perkhuli is a predominantly male Georgian folk round dance; its name comes from 'pekhi' (foot) (Wikipedia). Of at least 20 versions, the 'multi-level' perkhuli is among the most popular, with one group of dancers standing on another group's shoulders to music in 3/4 time; another version alternates slow and fast rounds in 4/4. The northwestern mountain region of Svaneti is especially rich in perkhuli repertoire. Often described as the ritual forebearer of all Georgian folk choreography, it is danced with songs and shouts and welcomes participants of any number (georgia.travel).
card.insight: Perkhuli was inscribed on the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Georgia list in 2013 and is regarded as the foundational Georgian dance, its 'living towers' surviving in regional forms such as the Gurian Partsa (Wikipedia).
card.image_significance: Multi-tier round/tower dance. A representative image shows upright carriage, sweeping arm lines and embroidered dress — mountains, Georgia.
